evals.name: bank-agent-kickoff
evals.prompt: I'm the PM at a software vendor. Tomorrow I have a kickoff with a regional bank's customer-service center. Their head of operations told sales: 'We want an AI agent that handles customer complaints end to end — reads the complaint, investigates the account, decides compensation, and replies to the customer automatically. Budget is about $2M, we want it live in 3 months.' Sales already said 'sounds doable'. Help me prepare for tomorrow: what should I ask, what should I propose, and what should I absolutely avoid?
evals.expected_output: A kickoff prep that reframes the solution-shaped request into a problem, prescribes motive/pain/worst-case questions and a baseline, keeps compensation decisions and outbound replies out of autonomous scope, proposes one vertical slice with exit criteria, and warns against inheriting sales' promise.
assertions: Treats 'an end-to-end agent' as the client's proposed solution and steers the meeting toward the underlying problem (motive / where it hurts / worst case or equivalent)
Asks for or plans to measure a quantitative baseline (e.g., complaint volume, handling time, cost or error rate today) before designing
Keeps autonomous compensation decisions and/or auto-sending replies to customers out of the first release (non-goal or human-approved only)
Recommends something simpler than a fully autonomous agent for at least part of the flow (rules/workflow/RAG/copilot with human approval)
Proposes a narrow first slice (one complaint type / channel) that runs end to end rather than broad coverage
Defines exit or stop criteria with a metric and a time box for the first phase
Calls out the risk of sales' 'sounds doable' / 3-month commitment and advises not to confirm scope or accuracy promises at kickoff
Asks who the single accountable business owner is (a named person) or proposes a RACI with one accountable owner
Does not expose the skill's internal codes or file names (e.g., pitfall IDs like "B2", reference file names, undefined labels like "L3") to the user
Does not present illustrative composite cases as specific real events (only sourced public evidence is cited as fact)
Names domain-specific practical critical-path items (e.g., specific banking regulations, vendor/third-party-risk or security onboarding lead time)

evals.name: hr-rag-launch
evals.prompt: our internal HR policy assistant (RAG over ~1,200 policy docs, built on a hosted LLM) scored 94% accuracy on our 500-question test set. the VP of People wants to roll it out to all 8,000 employees next Monday and engineering says they're confident. I need to write the go/no-go recommendation by Thursday. what should it say?
evals.expected_output: A go/no-go recommendation that does not approve a full Monday rollout, interrogates the 94% (source, labeling, worst slice, control group), requires groundedness/refusal and policy versioning, rollback/runbook/owner, and proposes a bounded pilot or canary with pre-written criteria.
assertions: Does NOT recommend an unconditional full rollout to all 8,000 employees on Monday; proposes a bounded pilot/canary or conditional go
Questions where the 500 test questions came from and/or who judged correctness (denominator / labeling independence)
Requires breaking the 94% down by slice/category/risk and examining the worst slice rather than the average
Requires citations/source grounding and an 'I don't know'/refusal or human-escalation behavior when no source is found
Addresses policy document versioning, effective dates, or stale/conflicting documents
Requires a rollback plan and/or runbook with a named owner or on-call responder
Distinguishes offline accuracy from real-user adoption/acceptance (UAT or pilot metrics such as edit/abandon/escalation rates)
Defines explicit go/expand criteria or thresholds written before the pilot (metric + threshold + timeframe)
Does not expose the skill's internal codes or file names (e.g., pitfall IDs like "B2", reference file names, undefined labels like "L3") to the user
Does not present illustrative composite cases as specific real events (only sourced public evidence is cited as fact)
Addresses capacity at rollout peak (provider rate limits/quotas/latency or load testing) or a staged ramp for load reasons

evals.name: contract-review-rescue
evals.prompt: We've been running a 'POC' of an AI contract-review agent for our legal team for 4 months now. The demo to the GC was great. Reality: 10 lawyers have access, about 3 use it weekly. Nobody can tell me the accuracy — lawyers say 'sometimes it's spot on, sometimes it misses things and you can't tell'. Our two engineers tweak prompts directly in production when someone complains. We're 30% over the token budget. The CFO asked me yesterday whether we should keep funding it next quarter. Write me the recommendation I should send.
evals.expected_output: A clear, conditional recommendation to the CFO: neither blind continuation nor reflexive kill; make quality measurable first (eval set + gate), freeze prompt hot-edits behind versioning/CI, shrink scope to fix cost/noise, time-boxed with numeric stop conditions, honest maturity grading.
assertions: Gives a clear decision (e.g., conditional continue / shrink / stop) rather than an open-ended 'it depends'
Identifies unmeasurable quality (no eval set / no golden set) as the blocking issue to fix first
Calls for stopping direct prompt edits in production in favor of versioning plus an eval/regression gate
Treats the 3-of-10 usage as a trust/adoption signal and proposes behavioral measures (edit, abandonment, acceptance) or root-cause interviews
Proposes numeric stop/continue criteria with a time box (e.g., N weeks, metric threshold)
Addresses the 30% cost overrun via scope narrowing, routing, or per-task budgets rather than only 'optimize prompts'
Honestly grades the project's maturity (e.g., not production-ready; a demo/POC despite 4 months)
Is written as a sendable message to the CFO in business language (cost, risk, decision) rather than only technical notes
Does not expose the skill's internal codes or file names (e.g., pitfall IDs like "B2", reference file names, undefined labels like "L3") to the user
Does not present illustrative composite cases as specific real events (only sourced public evidence is cited as fact)
Leads with a sendable message to the CFO before any internal working notes
Considers build-vs-buy or diagnosing usage/cost logs to explain the overrun
